# Enola CLI

> Enola CLI builds private infrastructure on Linux: self-hosted services that bind only to 127.0.0.1 and are reachable exclusively through the Tor network, with system hardening applied by default and releases verifiable offline. Deploy targets include Tor hidden services (.onion), Git servers (Forgejo), CMS platforms (WordPress, Drupal, Ghost, Magnolia, Strapi, Wagtail), anonymous file sharing, WireGuard VPN, UFW firewall and AppArmor sandboxing on Debian/Linux. Releases are signed with minisign (Ed25519) and post-quantum ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204).

Important notes:

- Source-visible proprietary software: free for personal, non-commercial use. No redistribution, no commercial use. See LICENSE.
- Security vulnerabilities must be reported privately to salvadorpalmarodriguez@gmail.com (coordinated disclosure, no public issues).
- Single binary `enola-cli`, requires root (sudo) for most operations. Runs on Debian/Linux with Docker, Nginx and Tor.

- [FAQ (EN)](https://salvadorpalmarodriguez.github.io/enola-cli-lite/en/faq): Frequently asked questions and troubleshooting

- [Verify downloads (EN)](https://salvadorpalmarodriguez.github.io/enola-cli-lite/en/verify-downloads): SHA256 + minisign + ML-DSA-65 verification guide
- [MCP server (EN)](https://salvadorpalmarodriguez.github.io/enola-cli-lite/en/commands-mcp): Model Context Protocol server for AI agents

MCP security: read-only by default. Mutations require `--allow-write` and may
be restricted with `--allow-tools`; destructive operations additionally
require `force: true` and a single-use `confirm_token` bound to the exact
arguments (300-second lifetime). `try_run: true` validates and simulates
without side effects. `enola_run_command` uses typed argv and never dispatches
the `mcp`, `ask`, `ssh`, `uninstall`, `web` or `setup` families, nor the
`update apply`, `test run` or `test benchmark` paths. When running with
elevated privileges, fix argv, environment, policy source and audit-log
location in a trusted launcher; do not grant a wildcard sudo rule such as
`enola-cli mcp *`.

Local AI assistant (`enola-cli ask <prompt> [--model <m>] [--endpoint <url>] [--instance <name>] [--no-exec] [--yes]`):
connects to a local Ollama instance (`[ai]` in `~/.enola/config.toml` or env vars `ENOLA_AI_ENDPOINT`, `ENOLA_AI_MODEL`, `ENOLA_AI_TIMEOUT_SECS`; defaults `http://127.0.0.1:11434`, `llama3.1:8b`, `120s`) and reuses the `ToolRegistry`. Read-only tools execute directly; mutating and destructive tools require interactive `[s/N]` confirmation on TTY (or `--yes` for non-interactive use; fails closed without TTY) or `--no-exec` to simulate via `try_run` with zero side effects.

GGUF model library (`enola-cli ai model list|download|import|add|delete|validate|refresh`):
per-instance library at `/srv/enola-ai/<name>/ollama/models-gguf/` (visible inside Ollama as `/root/.ollama/models-gguf/`). `download` fetches `.gguf` from HuggingFace (`org/repo` + `--file`) or a direct URL with streaming, `Range` resume and SHA-256 check, then registers via `/api/create` unless `--no-register`; clearnet by default, `--tor`/`ENOLA_AI_USE_TOR_DOWNLOADS`/`[ai].use_tor_for_downloads` forces the SOCKS5h proxy and the egress route is reported. `add` pulls registry refs (`/api/pull`) or registers library files; `delete` requires `--force` (Destructive in MCP); `list`/`validate` are ReadOnly.

RAG index (`enola-cli ai rag status|ingest|bind|sync|config`): per-instance vector store container (`enola-ai-<n>-chromadb` or `-qdrant`) lazily provisioned via `ContainerPort` on `127.0.0.1` (port range 12001–12500, flock), volume `/srv/enola-ai/<n>/<backend>/`, limits 1 GiB/512 pids. `ingest` chunks docs/code with boundary-aware overlap (presets docs|code|faq|large) and embeds via the instance Ollama (`/api/embed`, `nomic-embed-text`, deterministic hash fallback). `bind` registers sources (`git|filesystem|wordpress`, canonicalized, system dirs rejected) and is Destructive in MCP (requires `--force`); `sync` re-ingests (`git pull` as invoking user, WP REST for wordpress). `docs_lookup` MCP tool queries the `enola_docs` collection semantically when a vector store is provisioned (optional alternative to `docs_search`).

Local AI instances (`enola-cli ai create|list|status|start|stop|delete|publish|hide|logs`):
manages isolated Ollama (`enola-ai-<name>-ollama`) and Open WebUI (`enola-ai-<name>-webui`) containers over `ContainerPort` (Bollard), bound exclusively to `127.0.0.1` with calibrated resource limits (`memory_limit >= 8 GiB`, `pids_limit >= 4096`), `flock` port reservation, NVIDIA GPU passthrough via `EnolaHardwareProbe`, and `.onion` publication via Nginx + Tor.

Development-only escape hatches (never in production, never via `sudo -E`):
`ENOLA_AUTO_SETUP=1` (non-TTY preflight auto-installs deps),
`ENOLA_ALLOW_UNSIGNED_UPDATE=1` / `--allow-unsigned` (skips minisign
verification), `ENOLA_SKIP_ROOT_CHECK=1`, `ENOLA_MINISIGN_BIN`,
`ENOLA_WEB_TOKEN`, `ENOLA_UPDATE_*` trust-anchor overrides (at euid 0 require
`ENOLA_UPDATE_ENV_ANCHORS=1`, and `[update]` is read only from root-owned
`/etc/enola/config.toml`). Root processes evaluate them with a visible warning.
Full table in config-reference.md "Variables solo-desarrollo".
